name: Edinburgh Regatta
body:
The Forth’s main inter-club keelboat weekend, based at Granton. In 2026 it was run as a single Saturday: three round-the-cans races for handicap fleets plus a cruiser passage race.

This is exactly the kind of date that should sit on a shared Forth picture — visiting boats, extra rib traffic, and pontoon demand at Granton on the same weekend the commercial Forth is still working.

Dates move. The working group’s job is that the card is owned by the host clubs, not copied from last year’s notice of race.
facts:
Hosts ~ RFYC + FCYC
2026 Date ~ Sat 22 August (one day)
Fleets ~ Fast / slow handicap + cruiser passage
Berthing ~ Edinburgh Marina pontoon

name: RFYC One Design Regatta
body:
Granton one-design weekend, usually mid-September. In 2026: 19–20 September. Home event for the Scottish Dragon fleet and visiting one-designs.

Two days of racing in the Granton patch. Useful to have on the shared calendar so small harbours and FTNS know there is a concentrated leisure fleet mid-Firth that weekend.
facts:
Hosts ~ Royal Forth Yacht Club
2026 Date ~ 19–20 September
Fleets ~ Dragon and other one-designs

name: PEYC 707 Sprints
body:
Open 707 weekend at Port Edgar. 2026 dates: 3–4 October, with shore-side racing hospitality. Port Edgar has also hosted the 707 Nationals — four days, 20-plus boats, racing in the shadow of the bridges.

This event sits in the busiest visual and traffic corridor on the Forth. A shared pin here is how yacht clubs talk to Forth Ports and cruise planners before the weekend, not after a near-miss write-up.
facts:
Host ~ Port Edgar Yacht Club
2026 date ~ 3–4 October
Water ~ Queensferry Bay, under the bridges

name: ELYC Open & Keelboat Regattas
body:
East Lothian’s two headline opens: the club regatta (dinghy and yacht classes, often eight races over a weekend) and a separate keelboat regatta. ELYC also takes class nationals — visiting fleets fill the harbour and the town.

Courses use the club’s published racing marks off North Berwick. Wind against the outgoing Forth can make the outer marks serious water. The working-group card should carry the mark chart link and a “visitor berth / trailer park” line owned by the club.
facts:
Host ~ East Lothian Yacht Club
Water ~ Off North Berwick, Bass Rock courses
Pattern ~ Summer open + keelboat weekend

name: Club evening series
body:
The ordinary Forth racing week, not the trophy weekend. Royal Forth evening series (often Wednesday and Thursday) and Port Edgar twilight handicap. Small boats, short courses, daylight that shrinks after August.

These are the dates commercial operators never see and clubs assume everyone knows. Putting a single recurring card on the shared picture is the cheapest win in the first 90 days — “there is racing off Granton and Port Edgar on weekday evenings, April to September.”
facts:
RFYC ~ Wed / Thu evenings, 18:30 typical
PEYC ~ Twilight handicap series
Season ~ April lift-in to September

name: Passage races & cruise-in-company
body:
Longer Forth races and cruises-in-company that actually use the small harbours this working group is for. FCYC and RFYC send boats east to Anstruther, Dunbar and Eyemouth. A club “race in company” is not a regatta — it is a fleet arriving at a working harbour on a Saturday afternoon.

The card the group should write: date, expected numbers, who talks to the harbourmaster, where trailers and ribs go. That is the interrogation small operators asked for.
facts:
Typical Ends ~ Anstruther, Dunbar, Eyemouth
Need ~ Visitor berths + harbour notice
Also ~ RFYC cruise-and-race-in-company

name: East Coast Sailing Week
body:
A multi-day east-coast week that rotates between the Forth, the Tay and Northumberland. When it is the Forth’s year the estuary sees a visiting fleet for several days, not a single Saturday.

This is a working-group item rather than a fixed pin: next Forth year, host clubs, harbours used, and how early Forth Ports / FTNS hear about it.
facts:
Organiser ~ East-coast clubs via FYCA pattern
Forth Year ~ Every third year
Scale ~ Visiting fleets, multi-day
